subject: Re: Dedicated onboarding — scaling validation & cutover window
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@tidecloud.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@tidecloud.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity check before we sign

Diego — thanks again for the demo yesterday. TideCloud is excited to move from a Hosted pilot to Dedicated. Before legal/procurement signs off we need a clear validation run and a suggested cutover window so we can coordinate infra and app teams.

Attached is our 30-day token/req distribution and a short spike of peak-hour traces. High-level asks:
- Confirm the GPU instance footprint you recommend for our live traffic (avg 130 rps, p95 420ms generation latency target)
- A short validation plan (staging runs) and suggested 48–72h cutover windows with rollback steps
- Any temporary capacity limits we should expect during the initial 2 weeks post-cutover

Sasha (product) and procurement are looped — can you share a timeline by EOD Monday?

Thanks,
Evan
Director of Platform — TideCloud
[Attachment: tidecloud-metrics-202608.xlsx (xlsx, 160KB)]

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@tidecloud.com>
Cc: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@tidecloud.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity check before we sign

Evan — thanks for the file and the clear asks. Short answer: yes, we can provide a validated sizing and a conservative cutover window. Longer answer below and a proposed cadence.

High-level proposal (summary):
- Validation: 72h staged validation in a Dedicated staging pool that mirrors your expected production mix (we will run continuous-fanout load tests against your endpoint and measure p95 latencies).
- Sizing: initial allocation = 6x A10G-equivalent cards (quantized model stack) with room to burst 2x for short peaks — this meets the 130 rps baseline with p95 headroom based on the sample metrics you provided.
- Cutover window: 48h rolling cutover (can be done weekend). Day 1: staged traffic split 10/90 -> 50/50 for smoke. Day 2: full traffic with 2h canary and immediate rollback to hosted if errors > 1.5% or p95 degradation > 40%.
- Post-cutover limits: we recommend a soft token cap for first 14 days to avoid noisy neighbors, automatically lifted based on SLA health.

Action items I’ll take now: share a concrete validation runbook and a deterministic timeline. Marissa — can you validate capacity procurement lead times with Dedicated ops? Ben — can you confirm the burst policy and autoscale thresholds we’d apply?

Diego
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Looping infra — quick notes:
- Procurement/Capacity lead time: 10 business days to reserve 6 A10G-equivalent in the us-west cluster, additional 5 days if we need the +2 burst reserved
- Staging pool: we can spin up a mirrored staging pool in 48 hours once we have the exact model artifact and quantization profile (request that from devs ASAP)
- Load test plan: recommend 3 phases — baseline, sustained 4-hour soak at 2x baseline, and spike test (20-minute 4x bursts)

Karthik — can you draft the runbook steps and the acceptance criteria (p95 threshold, error rate, throughput)? I’ll capture procurement ETA in the timeline doc.

Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity check — runbook & acceptance criteria (draft)

Draft runbook (excerpt):
1) Preflight (Day -7 to -3):
   - Confirm model artifact hash and quantization settings; store artifact in private registry.
   - Provision staging pool (6 A10G-equivalent) and deploy same inference stack as prod.
   - Sanity smoke: <1% error, p95 < 600ms on baseline replay.
2) Validation (Day -2 to 0):
   - Phase A: Baseline traffic replay (24h). Acceptance: p95 <= 1.2x planned target and error rate < 0.5%.
   - Phase B: Soak (4h at 2x baseline). Acceptance: no sustained queue/backpressure; autoscaler behaves as configured.
   - Phase C: Spike (20m at 4x baseline). Acceptance: graceful degradation, tail latency under 2x p95 baseline, no system-level OOMs or kernel restarts.
3) Cutover (Day 1 to 2):
   - Day 1 morning: 10% traffic to Dedicated for smoke; monitor 4h.
   - Day 1 afternoon: 50% split for production-like behavior, 8h watch.
   - Day 2: 100% after 2h canary if all health metrics green. Rollback plan: route back to Hosted API and scale down Dedicated; we keep the cache primed for fast fallback.
4) Post-cutover (Day 3 to 14):
   - Enforce soft token cap (configurable) and expand after 7 days of stable metrics.
   - Daily health syncs with TideCloud for week 1, then cadence to 3x/week.

Acceptance thresholds (short): p95 target 420ms; go/no-go if p95 > 588ms or error rate > 1.5% sustained over 30m.

Ben — I'll need the exact autoscaler and cache-warming knobs for the timeline doc.

Karthik
Principal Infra SWE — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T11:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity check — autoscale & burst policy

Quick on policy:
- Autoscale baseline: maintain target utilization ~70% token throughput; scale step = +1 GPU per 10% sustained over 5m, max scaling velocity = 2 GPUs per 10m to avoid noisy churn.
- Burst policy: allow instantaneous +2 GPUs (short-lived) for 30m, subject to on-call ops approval for anything beyond 30m. Billing note: bursts billed at on-demand premium during first 14 days (as discussed on the deal).
- Cache-warm: we will preheat KV cache during smoke tests; expected warm-up time ~18–24h for steady hit ratio.

Attaching deployment architecture figure and I'll add these knobs to the runbook.

Ben
Infra Reliability Lead — Redwood Inference

Team — this is exactly what we needed, thank you. Procurement is good with the 10 business day reservation and the short-term burst billing note. A couple quick confirmations before we finalize the SOW:
- Confirm the exact dates you can reserve the staging pool (we prefer Sept 20–23 for validation; cutover the following weekend Sept 25–26).
- We’ll ask our engineering team to push the quantized model artifact by EOD Sept 3 to the private registry you provide.
- Please flag any assumptions (e.g., average request length, prompt conditioning that could change token counts).

Once those dates are confirmed we’ll circulate the SOW to legal. Appreciate the clear rollback plan — that made procurement comfortable.

Evan
Director of Platform — TideCloud
